post.author: Brandon Smith
post.topic_summary: Industrial systems need explicit contracts, observable state, and clear system boundaries to become AI-ready; hidden structure (not complexity) is what makes systems hard to operate and improve.

comment_posted.comment_text:
The "hidden structure" framing is accurate. A system that technically works but doesn't expose itself clearly creates a whole class of problems that look like complexity but are really opacity.

The practical fix in industrial environments usually comes down to two things together: a defined payload schema at the edge (SparkplugB or something equivalent) and a semantic layer above the protocol data that makes state inspectable without reading native PLC registers. When those two exist, the frozen-project problem starts to break down. You can add tooling, swap analytics platforms, or build AI context against the same underlying state without renegotiating every integration point.
